result.summary: Rework for the BLOCKER in handoffs/WF02-REQ-019/step-02b-reviewer.json: with zero active chapters, assignChapterOrPrompt returns "continue" but users.chapter_id stays permanently NULL, so advanceOnboarding always re-derives hasChapter as false and returns "chapter-needed" -- an outcome makeStartHandler and makeConsentCallbackHandler had no branch for, so both silently stopped replying right after the noActiveChapters message (no greeting, no profile prompt, forever). Re-read docs/agents/design/REQ-019.md §3.2/§3.3 in full and diffed the current apps/bot/src/handlers/start.ts against the pre-REQ-019 version (git show d7458ae~1:apps/bot/src/handlers/start.ts) as instructed: confirmed the old makeStartHandler unconditionally sent start.greeting immediately after the chapter-assignment block regardless of whether chapterId ended up set (1 chapter) or stayed null (0 chapters) -- so 'noActiveChapters is itself the terminal reply' was never the old behavior; 'the flow always keeps moving past the chapter step' was. FIX (apps/bot/src/handlers/start.ts, makeStartHandler and makeConsentCallbackHandler only -- makeChapterCallbackHandler needed no change, since it only ever fires once a chapter WAS actually assigned): both call sites now track a local `hasChapter` boolean, seeded from `flowUser.chapterId !== null`. When it starts false and assignChapterOrPrompt is run, a "continue" result (whether because exactly one chapter got silently assigned OR because zero active chapters exist and there was never a chapter to assign) now sets `hasChapter = true` before calling advanceOnboarding, instead of re-deriving hasChapter from the (still-null, in the zero-chapters case) chapterId afterward. This mirrors the exact same treatment handlers/profile.ts's own reachReadyOrPrompt helper already applies for its call sites (that helper's own header comment already documents this precedent -- REVIEWER's finding pointed at exactly this asymmetry between profile.ts and start.ts). With this fix, advanceOnboarding is called with the chapter step correctly marked resolved, so it proceeds to whatever comes next (a profile question for an incomplete profile, or the greeting once ready) instead of returning the unhandled "chapter-needed" literal a second time. No change to domain/onboarding.ts, domain/profile.ts, or handlers/profile.ts -- REVIEWER's own diagnosis (and my independent re-read) placed this entirely in start.ts's two call sites, which is where the fix landed. TEST (new file, apps/bot/src/handlers/start.test.ts): the first DB-backed automated test in this codebase (every prior *.test.ts is pure-function only). Builds a real grammY Bot wired to the actual exported makeStartHandler/makeChapterCallbackHandler/makeConsentCallbackHandler against a real Postgres connection, with network replaced by a bot.api.config.use(...) transformer that captures every outgoing call and fabricates its response (no token, no real Telegram call, no getMe() -- botInfo is pre-supplied). Two cases, both seeding zero rows in `chapters` (TRUNCATEd in beforeEach): (1) a brand-new user dispatched through /start then the consent:agree callback -- asserts the captured sequence is exactly [sendMessage consent.prompt] then [answerCallbackQuery, sendMessage noActiveChapters, sendMessage profile.promptFirstName], proving makeConsentCallbackHandler's own chapter-needed branch no longer dead-ends. (2) a returning user seeded directly via resolveOrCreateUser+recordConsent (consent already recorded, no chapter) dispatched through /start directly -- asserts [sendMessage noActiveChapters, sendMessage profile.promptFirstName], proving makeStartHandler's own chapter-needed branch no longer dead-ends. Both tests fail against the pre-fix code (confirmed by re-running them against a stash of the pre-fix start.ts: the second sendMessage in each case never arrives) and pass against the fix. The suite self-skips (via vitest's per-test ctx.skip(), not a hard failure) when it cannot reach TEST_DATABASE_URL (defaults to apps/bot's own docker-compose.yml dev DB, postgres://bot:bot@localhost:55432/bot) or that DB has not been migrated -- flagged as an infrastructure gap, not silently worked around: .github/workflows/ci-cd.yml's Test step runs `npm test` with no Postgres service, so this suite (and any future DB-backed test) only actually executes locally today. Recommend ORCH route a follow-up to add a postgres:16-alpine service to the ci-cd.yml build job. LIVE VERIFICATION (both scenarios the task named, dispatched via real bot.handleUpdate() against a real scratch Postgres I stood up myself -- apps/bot/docker-compose.yml, docker compose up -d, DATABASE_URL=postgres://bot:bot@localhost:55432/bot npx drizzle-kit migrate, migrations applied cleanly): a throwaway script (apps/bot/scratch-verify-rework1.ts, deleted after use, git status --porcelain confirmed clean before writing this handoff) reproduced both exactly: - Fresh user /start -> consent:agree, zero active chapters: after /start, exactly one reply (consent.prompt). After consent:agree: [answerCallbackQuery, sendMessage 'Отделения пока недоступны.' (start.noActiveChapters), sendMessage 'Как вас зовут (имя)?' (profile.promptFirstName)] -- no dead end. - Returning user, consent already recorded (seeded directly via resolveOrCreateUser+recordConsent), no chapter, zero active chapters, direct /start: [sendMessage 'Отделения пока недоступны.', sendMessage 'Как вас зовут (имя)?'] -- no dead end. Both match the automated test's own assertions exactly. docker compose down -v torn down after. COMMANDS RUN, REAL OUTPUT: - npm run lint (repo root) -> 0 errors (2 pre-existing, unrelated apps/web LCP warnings; one eslint no-unused-directive warning I introduced and then fixed in the same pass, confirmed gone on re-run). - npm run build (repo root, both workspaces) -> Next.js build compiled successfully; tsc -p tsconfig.json for apps/bot clean. - npx vitest run (repo root, the canonical invocation -- this is the command vitest.config.ts's own exclude: ['**/dist/**'] comment documents as the one that avoids double-counting apps/bot's tsc-compiled dist/**/*.test.js copies): with no scratch Postgres running, 13 files / 142 passed + 2 skipped (144) -- the 2 new DB tests skip cleanly, no failures. With scratch Postgres up and migrated, re-ran the same command: 13 files / 144 passed, 0 skipped -- both new tests pass for real. NOTE on the '284' figure in step-02b-reviewer.json: that count was produced with `npx vitest run --root apps/bot`, which (confirmed by direct inspection) does NOT apply the repo-root vitest.config.ts's dist/ exclude when --root is overridden, so it double-counts every test once from src/ and once from apps/bot/dist/ (12 unique files x2 = 24, 142 unique tests x2 = 284 -- exactly matching the 142-test floor BACKEND-DEV originally reported). I reproduced this myself: running --root apps/bot with a live DB, the dist/ and src/ copies of my new DB test raced each other against the SAME real Postgres tables (both truncate/insert against tg_id 900000000 independently) and one copy failed with a length-mismatch, not because the fix is wrong (the src/ copy passed every time) but because two independent module instances of the same test file were mutating the same live database concurrently -- an artifact of the dist-duplication bug, not of this rework. The canonical `npx vitest run` from repo root (no --root override, matching vitest.config.ts's own documented purpose) is unaffected and is what I used to confirm growth: 142 unique tests before this rework, 144 after (both new). No new deviation from the design introduced. No schema change. No file touched outside apps/bot/src/handlers/start.ts (fix), apps/bot/src/handlers/start.test.ts (new test), and this handoff.

npm run lint (repo root) -> exit 0, 0 errors (2 pre-existing unrelated apps/web warnings)
npm run build (repo root) -> exit 0, Next.js build + tsc -p tsconfig.json for apps/bot both clean
npx vitest run (repo root, no Postgres running) -> 13 files / 142 passed + 2 skipped (144), 0 failures
cd apps/bot && docker compose up -d; DATABASE_URL=postgres://bot:bot@localhost:55432/bot npx drizzle-kit migrate -> migrations applied successfully
npx vitest run (repo root, Postgres up+migrated) -> 13 files / 144 passed, 0 skipped, 0 failures -- both new DB-backed tests pass for real

npx tsx apps/bot/scratch-verify-rework1.ts (fresh user /start+consent:agree, and returning-already-consented-no-chapter direct /start, both against zero active chapters) -> both reach profile.promptFirstName after start.noActiveChapters, no dead end -- script deleted after use
docker compose down -v; git status --porcelain -> clean, no stray files before writing this handoff

ac_results.ZERO_ACTIVE_CHAPTERS_REGRESSION: FIXED and locked down -- both makeStartHandler's own chapterId===null branch and makeConsentCallbackHandler's own chapterId===null branch now fall through to advanceOnboarding with the chapter step correctly marked resolved, reaching the first profile prompt (or greeting once ready) instead of dead-ending after noActiveChapters. Covered by a new automated test (apps/bot/src/handlers/start.test.ts) and independently reproduced live via bot.handleUpdate() against a real scratch Postgres.

issues.description: .github/workflows/ci-cd.yml's `Test` step (npm test) runs with no Postgres service, so apps/bot/src/handlers/start.test.ts's new DB-backed cases self-skip in CI today (they only run when TEST_DATABASE_URL/apps/bot's own docker-compose.yml dev DB is reachable and migrated). Recommend ORCH route a follow-up to add a postgres:16-alpine service to the ci-cd.yml build job so this suite (and any future DB-backed test) actually executes in CI rather than only locally.
